items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now this happened all on one day. Marty Cosa. Jack, was that before the turn of the century, or after?

ctx.x: Like a hadicol, huh? Yeah, something like an antiseptic, you feel. And, uh, from there, from there, we jumped in a wagon and played, uh, an hour and a half, again, for the Merry Whitties Ball.
Now this happened all on one day. Marty Cosa. Jack, was that before the turn of the century, or after?

After. Uh, then I played, uh, the advertisement of the Merry Whitties Ball. And from there, we jumped up to, uh, St. Charles and Calliope and played the Day Parade. And from the Day Parade, we came all the way down to Frenchman Street, and we played the View of Damascus on Frenchman and Decatur. And from the Frenchman and Decatur, we jumped again in the, in the, uh, wagon, and finished our job playing the advertising for the Merry Whitties Ball.
